#1 Title Slide cover

Building Access in IdentityNow

A comprehensive architectural blueprint detailing identity generation, profile configuration, account correlation, access modeling, role engineering, and dynamic lifecycle governance.

Notes: Welcome to Building Access in IdentityNow: Identity Model Components and Access Model. This presentation provides an end-to-end technical breakdown of how identities are modeled, aggregated from authoritative sources, correlated with target accounts, structured into access profiles and roles, and dynamically governed through lifecycle state transitions.
#2 Three Columns architecture

Identity Model Components

The fundamental building blocks governing digital persona and target system permissions
Core Entities
Who You Are
Identity

A representation of a person or service and all the information associated with them. This includes security-relevant information as well as current status in the organization.

Where You Exist
Account

A representation of an identity on a source system. This user account contains information about the identity and may also contain accesses as well.

What You Can Do
Access

Securities which grant accounts an ability to perform actions. They define what a user can and can't do in a system. On a source these may be known as entitlements, authorizations, groups, rights, permissions. Access can also be defined through roles and access profiles.

Notes: Baseline Slide 2 defines the three core pillars: Identity, Account, and Access. Identities represent the human or service entity, accounts represent presence on individual systems, and access defines effective operational rights.
#3 Title and Content architecture

Identity, Account & Access Architecture

Relational mapping connecting central identities to target accounts and granular access
Entity Relationships

Central identities govern accounts across target sources. Users never log into target systems as identities; identities govern accounts which hold native access permissions.

#4 Title and Content architecture

Reading from Leading HR Source

Source System Schema, Account Aggregation, and Identity Profile Attribute Mapping
Ingestion Pipeline

Authoritative systems serve as Systems of Record. The ingestion pipeline reads raw source data (id, firstName, lastName, email, active, location, country, ssn), generates account objects, applies identity mappings, and populates the central identity.

#5 Four Tiles process

Building Identities

Four-step administrative workflow for establishing authoritative identity ingestion
Setup Sequence
Connections
1. Create Authoritative Source

Navigate to Admin > Connections > Sources > +New. Establish connection parameters and service account credentials to the primary HR system of record.

Identities
2. Create Identity Profile

Navigate to Admin > Identities > Identity Profiles > +New. Generate the governance template that binds source accounts to identity records.

Policy & Mappings
3. Configure Identity Profile

Associate Identity Profile with Source. Define identity mappings, transform logic, sign-in methods, and authentication policies.

Data Import
4. Aggregate Accounts

Navigate to Admin > Connections > Sources > Import Data tab > Import Accounts. Ingest source records to trigger initial identity generation.

Notes: Baseline Slide 5 outlines the step-by-step procedural sequence to build identities in IdentityNow: create source, create profile, configure mappings, aggregate accounts.
#6 Four Tiles architecture

Identity Profiles

Core governance configuration rules and priority ordering mechanics
Governance Rules
Foundation
Identity Template & Policy

An identity profile is a template for creating identities, and a central place where identity policy is defined.

Personas
Identity Type Alignment

Commonly aligned to identity type (e.g. Employees, Contractors, Students, Faculty) to define distinct lifecycle paths.

Exclusivity
Single-Profile Assignment

An identity can only be assigned by a single identity profile at any given time. Configured in Admin > Identities > Identity Profiles.

Precedence
Priority & Ordering

Enforces implicit priority / ordering in the user interface. Precedence can also be adjusted programmatically via REST APIs.

Notes: Baseline Slide 6 defines the strict single-profile constraint: an identity can only be assigned by one identity profile. Highlight that ordering in the UI dictates precedence during account evaluation.
#7 Four Tiles security

Identity Profile Settings

Authentication parameters, network access boundaries, and credential policies
Policy Definition
System of Record
Account Source

Defines the authoritative account source that seeds identity records and establishes profile identity mappings.

Authentication
Sign-in Method

Defines authentication for the user (e.g. IdentityNow direct sign-in or delegated Active Directory).

Access Policy
Network Boundaries

Enforces Off-Network sign-in restrictions, conditional access, and Untrusted Geographies blocking or step-up verification.

MFA Enforcement
Strong Authentication

Enforces multi-factor authentication (MFA) and strong credential requirements during user sign-in.

Notes: Baseline Slide 7 establishes settings policies: account source binding, sign-in method, off-network access rules, untrusted geographies filtering, and strong authentication enforcement.

#14 Title and Content architecture

Target Accounts Correlation to Identities

Matching uncorrelated accounts from downstream applications to central identities
Target Aggregation

Target application accounts are ingested and processed through the correlation engine. Deterministic correlation rules (e.g. employeeId, email, username) bind uncorrelated accounts to central identities. Unmatched accounts remain uncorrelated for administrative remediation.

Bridging the Business Access Model with native IT source system permissions
Model Hierarchy

#16 Four Tiles architecture

Building Blocks: Entitlements

Granular permissions, group memberships, and allocate-able access units
Building Blocks
Ingestion
Source Aggregation

Aggregated directly from connected target sources (Active Directory, SAP, SaaS).

Permissions
Operational Access

Represent individual allocate-able points of operational access and granular rights.

Containers
Profile Bundling

Bundled into access profiles strictly for a single connected target source system.

Governance
Role Assignment Criteria

Evaluated as membership criteria during automated role assignment and account scanning.

Notes: Baseline Slide 16 defines Entitlements: aggregated from source, individual points of access, bundled into APs for a single source, evaluated as role criteria, and detected via account scanning.

Extracting native group objects and permissions into the IdentityNow catalog
Catalog Aggregation

Source systems expose native groups and permissions (e.g. Group1 'FieldOps'). Connectors map these via entitlement schemas into the central IdentityNow catalog, making them governable.

#18 Four Tiles architecture

Building Blocks: Access Profiles

Single-source entitlement bundling, request governance, and equivalency detection
Building Blocks
Scope Constraint
Single-Source Bundling

Bundle one or more entitlements strictly from a single source system to represent cohesive operational access.

Request Center
Request Governance

Can be requested directly by end users through the IdentityNow Request Center with optional approval workflows.

Detection Engine
Automated Detection

IDN compares aggregated accounts and entitlements against access profiles to detect held access automatically.

State Transition
Active State Marking

If an identity holds all bundled entitlements, the access profile is automatically detected and marked active.

Notes: Baseline Slide 18 details Access Profiles: must be single-source, requestable in Request Center with optional approval, and automatically detected when an identity holds all component entitlements.
#19 Four Tiles architecture

Building Blocks: Roles

Multi-source business packaging and automated membership assignment criteria
Building Blocks
Business Packaging
Multi-Source Bundling

Bundle access profiles across single or multiple connected sources into cohesive business access structures.

Organizational
Business Personas

Represent recognizable jobs, business personas, and organizational functions across the enterprise.

Membership Criteria
Model-Based Assignment

Automated membership matching criteria assign roles dynamically (e.g. title == 'Accountant' assigns Accountant Role).

Multi-System
Simultaneous Granting

Roles grant all included access profiles simultaneously across connected systems without manual intervention.

Notes: Baseline Slide 19 introduces Roles: multi-source bundling, representing business jobs, and assigned automatically via membership criteria (e.g. title == 'Accountant').
#20 Four Tiles governance

Roles: Business Definition & Assignment

Business context, automated membership criteria, and zero-approval provisioning
Role Management
Context
Business Name & Description

Describes role purpose in clear business-friendly context for intuitive governance and discovery.

Standard Attributes
Membership Criteria Match

Assignment based on criteria: standard match of entitlement, identity, or account attributes across sources.

Zero-Approval
Automated Fulfillment

Once criteria match, IdentityNow automatically provisions component access profiles with no approval process required.

Request Center
Requestable Role Options

Roles can also be made requestable in the Request Center with configured multi-tier approval chains.

Notes: Baseline Slide 20 emphasizes that criteria-based role assignment requires NO approval process, automatically provisioning access profiles when users meet attribute criteria.
#21 Four Tiles lifecycle

Building Blocks: Lifecycle States

State-driven access transitions and multi-source access profile automation
Building Blocks
Identity Profile
Employment State Models

Defined within Identity Profiles to represent employment stages (e.g. Pre-hire, Active, Leave, Terminated).

Multi-System
Multi-Source Access Granting

Combine and grant access profiles across multiple sources simultaneously based on the current lifecycle state.

Model-Based
State Transition Automation

Enforce automated provisioning and deprovisioning as users transition between lifecycle states.

Enforcement
Suspension & Revocation

Drive immediate access suspension or revocation when moving identities into inactive or terminated states.

Notes: Baseline Slide 21 covers Lifecycle States: defined in identity profiles, combining access profiles from multiple sources, and triggering automated access changes on state shifts.
#22 Title and Content architecture

Role Concept & Management Architecture

Hierarchical relationship connecting Business Roles, Technical Roles, and Applications
Role Architecture

Business Roles (R1, R2, R3) map to organizational attributes (OrgUnit, Job Role). Technical Roles (Access Profiles AP1, AP2, AP3) combine entitlements (E1..E6) from single sources, bounded by Application containers like Active Directory.

#23 Title and Content lifecycle

Building Block Relationships: Lifecycle States

Dynamic access assignment across Lifecycle State 1 (Active) and Lifecycle State 2 (Leave)
State Transitions

Identity Profiles define distinct lifecycle states. Transitioning between State 1 (Active) and State 2 (Leave) automatically adjusts assigned Access Profiles and Roles, revoking unnecessary access while maintaining identity integrity.

#24 Title and Content governance

Assignment vs Detection

Differentiating top-down governed provisioning from bottom-up source aggregation
Core Mechanics

Assigned access flows top-down via Role criteria or approved requests to trigger provisioning. Detected access is discovered bottom-up when source account aggregation reveals existing entitlements that match access profile bundles.

End-to-End Flow

#26 Four Tiles governance

Assignment: Special Circumstances

Approval bypass for criteria assignments and certification campaign boundaries
Governance Rules
Criteria Assignment
Zero-Approval Automation

When assigned via role membership criteria, no approval process is used as authoritative changes govern access.

Authoritative HR
Audited Consistency

System assumes HR attribute changes reflect authorized business events with complete audit trail integrity.

Certification Boundary
Campaign Exclusion Boundary

Access profiles granted to users by roles are not included in certification campaigns to avoid redundant review.

Top-Level Review
Role-Level Certification

Only the top-level Role is certified, streamlining reviewer workflows and preventing fatigue.

Notes: Baseline Slide 29 covers critical governance edge cases: criteria-based assignments bypass approvals, and access profiles granted via roles are excluded from individual certification campaigns.
#27 Four Tiles governance

Access Removal via Role & Edge Cases

Understanding automated deprovisioning triggers and critical non-deprovisioning behaviors
Deprovisioning
Automated Removal
Deprovisioning Triggers

Role-based deprovisioning removes entitlements when criteria no longer match or user is removed from identity list.

Critical Behavior
Role Editing Edge Case

No deprovisioning is triggered when a Role is edited to remove an Access Profile; granted access remains intact.

Critical Behavior
Role Deletion Behavior

Deleting a Role does NOT deprovision access previously assigned through it; target accounts retain permissions.

Governance Action
Explicit Cleanup Required

Removal requires explicit de-assignment or lifecycle transition to trigger target account deprovisioning.

Notes: Baseline Slide 30 highlights critical deprovisioning gotchas: editing a role to remove an access profile leaves existing access intact; deleting a role does NOT automatically deprovision granted access.
#28 Four Tiles architecture

Access Profiles and Roles Matrix

Cross-allocation relationships between multiple business roles and technical access profiles
Mapping Matrix
Multi-Role Reuse
Shared Profile Allocation

Roles R1 and R2 can share underlying Access Profiles (e.g. AP1, AP2) across distinct business departments.

Technical Packaging
Application Privilege Units

Access profiles package application-specific privileges into cohesive, manageable operational units.

Modular Architecture
Business & IT Decoupling

Decouples business role definitions from underlying IT infrastructure and target system changes.

Seamless Updates
Centralized Propagation

Modifying an access profile updates permissions for all parent business roles simultaneously.

Notes: Baseline Slide 31 diagrams the mapping matrix between Roles (R1, R2) and Access Profiles (AP1, AP2, AP3).

Lifecycle Integration
Profile Governance
Dynamic State Grants

Auto Provisioning
Automated Lifecycle Shift

Moving into a new lifecycle state automatically provisions required access and revokes obsolete access.

Authoritative Source
Master Template Foundation

Strict Alignment
HR to IT Synchronization

#31 Three Columns architecture

Each ONE Identity Can...

Core cardinality ratios governing identity relationships across the SailPoint platform
Cardinality Rules
1 : 0..N
Accounts & Sources

Each ONE Identity can possess multiple accounts across different connected target sources, but exactly ONE identity profile binds it to its authoritative source.

1 : 0..N
Roles & Access Profiles

Each ONE Identity can be assigned multiple Business Roles and multiple Access Profiles, granted via criteria, lifecycle state, or request.

1 : 0..N
Entitlements

Each ONE Identity can hold numerous individual entitlements, both assigned through governed access profiles and detected through direct account aggregation.

Notes: Baseline Slide 34 summarizes cardinality: Each ONE Identity can have multiple accounts, roles, access profiles, and entitlements.
